extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of media studies and journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Hartley's cultural-studies framework to analyze or produce news, using news values as shared semiotic codes between producers and audiences and attending to narrative, address, and audience understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: News depends on a culturally shared language / shared semiotic codes
rubrics_metrics.description: News depends for its effect on a culturally shared language. News values are shared semiotic codes between producers and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hartley's core approach: both producers and audiences participate in defining what counts as news; evaluation/production should attend to how meanings are coded and decoded in a given culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency / Time-Span
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that align with the news outlet's publication frequency or timing are more likely to be selected; temporal fit with editorial cycles matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events must meet a certain scale or significance threshold to merit coverage; assessors consider whether an event's magnitude crosses that threshold for the audience/outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unambiguity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer events and narratives that are unambiguous in meaning; ambiguous developments are less newsworthy unless reframed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningfulness (Cultural Proximity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories closer in cultural terms (values, norms, interests) to an audience are more meaningful and more likely to be reported and understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consonance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items that echo established schemas, stereotypes, or expectations resonate and are more readily selected as news; consonance interacts with unexpectedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpectedness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events that are surprising (but still intelligible within existing cultural frames) gain notice; balance between predictability and surprise increases newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing stories receive continued coverage; continuity increases salience and resource allocation for follow-up reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors compose a balanced 'news whole' across beats and topics; individual stories are selected to contribute to an overall composition or agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Elite Persons / Nations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories involving elites (prominent people or nations) are privileged because elites serve as salient signifiers for audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing events through individual protagonists/characters increases engagement and intelligibility; person-centered narratives are more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negativity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative events (conflict, disaster, scandal) attract attention and are often preferred in selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping reality through consensus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News constructs a version of reality based on shared agreements among producers and audiences; evaluators should notice how consensus shapes what is presented as 'real.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping dissents as outsiders
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissent is framed as outsider perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voices that dissent from consensus are often positioned as marginal or external; consider how news frames dissent and normalizes consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: The mode of address (how news speaks to its audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: How news speaks to its audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess or design the stance, tone, and rhetorical strategies by which news addresses readers/viewers (e.g., authoritative, conversational, pedagogical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common sense and audience understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Common sense assumptions guiding audience understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News relies on shared common-sense frameworks to make items intelligible; producers should exploit, and critics should interrogate, these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of news narrative — visual and verbal structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual and verbal structures that make up news narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to narrative elements (plotting, visuals, quotes, sequencing) and how they collaborate to produce meaning; both modes shape audience interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: News narrative vs. fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishing news narrative from fictional narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare and contrast techniques borrowed from fiction with the conventions that claim factuality in news; assess how narrative devices are used without collapsing into fiction.
